samples.text: A rain cloud forms when the air near the surface is warm enough to start condensing water vapor into clouds. As the warm air rises, it cools and the water vapor condenses into droplets, forming a cloud. This process continues until the cloud is large enough to hold rain, and the water begins to fall as rain. The formation of a rain cloud is primarily due to the presence of warm, moist air near the surface, which allows for the condensation of water vapor into clouds.
